correctness.rationale: For every integer m≥3, generic simplex-section vertices are in bijection with opposite-sign vertex pairs, giving N=K(m-K). Projected Gaussian normals have pair correlation −1/(m−1), so the angular bivariate normal sign law gives the exact finite-m expectation. A fully justified moving-threshold empirical-CDF expansion at the Gaussian sample mean gives a standard i.i.d. influence-function CLT with variance 1/4−1/(2π); continuous mapping and the exact mean expansion imply both asserted chi-square limits. All normalization and the m=3 boundary were checked; enumeration of 1,002 sign patterns and simulations provide separate finite corroboration, not proof of convergence.

originality.rationale: No equivalent or dominating theorem was identified after explicit Gaussian sign-count aliases, random regular-simplex section searches, published research-index queries and comparisons against the closest full-text geometric sources. De Loera–Lopez-Campos–Torres gives deterministic extremal counts; the published near-simplex result and the motivating manuscript concern volumes; Brown et al. treat infinite-mean rather than Gaussian sample-mean exceedances. This is bounded evidence of noncoverage, not a certification that an unindexed identity cannot exist.
residual_risks: The motivating 2026 regular-simplex central-volume preprint was only available at abstract level; its main statement is non-dominating but uninspected details create a residual originality uncertainty.
Older Gaussian residual-sign count, equicorrelated orthant, or stochastic-geometry literature may contain an equivalent expectation or asymptotic law without keywords captured in available indexes.
The 2021 heavy-tail statistical paper was compared through its precise surfaced theorem and assumptions, not a renewed complete source download.

value.rationale: The naturally motivated section-vertex count measures the combinatorial complexity of a Haar-random central simplex slice, a distinction absent from previously studied worst-case slice counts and minimum-volume sections. An exact expectation in all dimensions and the non-Gaussian order-m deficit law quantify how close generic slices lie to the deterministic balanced-sign maximum. The finite-m and asymptotic conclusions are structural results about a canonical infinite family, not an arbitrary numerical sample or a slight improvement to a constant.
